pages.text:
RHEUMNOTES
PSORIATIC ARTHRITIS
The GRAPPA Treatment Domains
SKIN PSORIASIS
Well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale. A core GRAPPA domain that drives treatment choice.
NAIL PSORIASIS
Nail-matrix and nail-bed disease: pitting, onycholysis, oil-drop change, and subungual hyperkeratosis.
DACTYLITIS
Uniform swelling of an entire digit from synovitis, tenosynovitis, and soft-tissue inflammation.
PERIPHERAL ARTHRITIS
Inflammatory synovitis of peripheral joints; oligo- or polyarticular, often asymmetric.
AXIAL DISEASE
Inflammation of the spine and sacroiliac joints causing inflammatory back pain and stiffness.
ENTHESITIS
Inflammation where tendons or ligaments insert into bone; commonly Achilles and plantar fascia.

pages.text:
RHEUMNOTES
PSORIATIC ARTHRITIS
PsA inflammation can affect joints, skin, nails, eyes, and the gut — and may lead to lasting damage if left untreated.
Skin / Psoriasis
Plaque psoriasis with silvery scale and underlying inflammation.
Eyes
Anterior uveitis with redness, pain, and sensitivity to light.
Gut
Inflammation in the gut, similar to IBD, with pain, bloating, or changes in bowel habits.
Shoulders
Shoulder joint and surrounding tissues can become inflamed and painful.
Wrists, Hands & Nails
Dactylitis (sausage finger), joint swelling, nail pitting, and onycholysis.
Feet / Enthesitis
Inflammation where tendons attach to bone, especially at the Achilles and plantar fascia.
Spine & SI Joints
Inflammation in the spine and sacroiliac joints can cause pain and stiffness.
Elbows
Elbow joints and surrounding tendons can become inflamed and tender.
Hips
Hip joints can be affected, leading to pain and reduced mobility.
Knees
Knee inflammation with swelling, warmth, and stiffness.
Ankles
Ankle and midfoot joints can become inflamed, causing pain and walking difficulty.

claims.reason: The title and introduction identify PsA and name skin, nails and joints. The draft retains possibility rather than inevitability.
The skin panel explicitly describes plaques with silvery scale; patches and scales preserve its meaning.
The nail panel lists pitting. Small pits describes this without adding other nail conditions.
The dactylitis panel says uniform swelling of an entire digit; finger or toe translates digit without adding a new symptom.
The clinical panel headed Wrists, Hands & Nails explicitly lists joint swelling.
The axial panel links inflammation to back pain and stiffness. The draft describes a possible symptom.
The enthesitis panel identifies inflammation where tendons or ligaments insert into bone. Attach is a plain-language equivalent of insert here.
The Feet / Enthesitis panel locates inflammation at tendon attachments in the feet. This refers to the preceding sentence's inflamed attachment sites.
The ankle panel explicitly lists pain and walking difficulty; the draft adds no treatment or urgency advice.
The knee panel lists swelling, warmth and stiffness; the draft makes no diagnosis or progression prediction.

quizzes.reason: Silvery scales are the unique skin answer; the other options describe different body areas. The skin panel supports the feedback.
Whole-digit swelling is explicit in the lesson and source. Nail pits and back pain do not answer the whole-digit question.
Source and lesson name bone as the attachment site; the other options do not match. Feedback adds no new claim.

coverage.reason: Silvery skin scales are explicitly taught.
Nail pitting is taught; lifting is an alternative example in the reference concept.
Whole-finger or whole-toe swelling is explicit.
Swollen hand joints are an example of joints away from the spine.
Back pain and stiffness are taught, but the draft does not separately teach nearby joint involvement.
Inflamed tendon or ligament attachments and a foot example are taught.

claims.reason: The introduction names eyes, gut and joints; can preserves uncertainty and does not predict individual symptoms.
The eye panel lists redness, pain and sensitivity to light. The draft describes symptoms without diagnosing uveitis.
The gut panel lists pain and bloating; painful and bloated preserve these meanings without diagnosing IBD.
Changes in bowel habits are explicitly present in the gut panel.
The shoulder panel names the joint and surrounding tissues as inflamed and painful. Sore preserves painful.
The hip panel states pain and reduced mobility. Harder to move translates reduced mobility without adding treatment.
Swelling, warmth and stiffness are listed in the knee panel.
The ankle panel includes ankle and midfoot inflammation. Middle of the foot translates midfoot.
The preceding sentence identifies ankle/midfoot inflammation; the same source explicitly states pain and walking difficulty.
The elbow panel describes inflamed and tender joints and surrounding tendons. Nearby preserves that location.
